newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end down as investors take profits.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end down as investors take profits.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed down Friday as investors took profits following two days of strong gains, brokers said.
They added, however, the market was likely to return to its upward trend early next week because players were expecting the release of good third quarter company results.
Friday, the General Index .IGRA fell 0.53 percent to 1,605.2 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL dropped 0.68 percent to 2,138.2 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
In a total of 2,488 operations, 41 stocks rose, 42 fell and 32 were stable in reduced volume of 37.1 million ($14.7 million).
"The profit-taking was expected by the market, especially in the brewery and public service sectors, after the recent big rises," said Maria Luisa Gonzalez of brokerage Godoy y Barclay.

The two breweries Compania Nacional de Cerveza Backus y Johnston, whose owners Grupo Backus are considering merging in a bid to boost their production, lost some of the ground they had gained this week.
Compania Nacional de Cerveza closed down 2.63 percent at 1.48 soles in volume of 1.59 million shares, while Backus dropped 0.68 percent to 2.90 soles on 824,000 shares.
Among other leaders, benchmark Telefonica del Peru fell 0.70 percent to 5.65 soles, accounting for ten percent of the day's volume.
Tele 2000 continued its dismal run and dropped 1.45 percent to 4.08 soles in low volume of 31,000 shares.
-- Claudia Guillen, Lima newsroom, 511 221-2134 REUTER SH
